after.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=0$ and ${x}_{2,3}=-1\pm 2\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=4.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =4(x-0)(x-(-1+2\text{i}))(x-(-1-2\text{i})) \\  & =4x(x-(-1+2\text{i}))(x-(-1-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4x(x-(-1+2\text{i}))(x-(-1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 4x({x}^{2}-x(-1-2\text{i})-x(-1+2\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(-1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 4x({x}^{2}+2x+5) & = \\ 4{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}+20x & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=4{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}+20x.$

The Argand diagram above shows the roots of the cubic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $4.$
content.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=0$ and ${x}_{2,3}=-1\pm 2\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=4.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =4(x-0)(x-(-1+2\text{i}))(x-(-1-2\text{i})) \\  & =4x(x-(-1+2\text{i}))(x-(-1-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4x(x-(-1+2\text{i}))(x-(-1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 4x({x}^{2}-x(-1-2\text{i})-x(-1+2\text{i})+(-1+2\text{i})(-1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 4x({x}^{2}+2x+5) & = \\ 4{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}+20x & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=4{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}+20x.$

after.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-2$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =2(x-(-2))(x-(-2))(x-5) \\  & =2(x+2)(x+2)(x-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+2)(x+2)(x-5) & =2({x}^{2}+4x+4)(x-5) \\  & =2({x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-5{x}^{2}+4x-20x-20) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-16x-20) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-32x-40.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-32x-40.$

content.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-2$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =2(x-(-2))(x-(-2))(x-5) \\  & =2(x+2)(x+2)(x-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+2)(x+2)(x-5) & =2({x}^{2}+4x+4)(x-5) \\  & =2({x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-5{x}^{2}+4x-20x-20) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-16x-20) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-32x-40.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-32x-40.$
